To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fusidic acid inhibits peptide-chain elongation by forming a stable ribosomal complex with the elongation factor G, and that this complex is able to form on ribosomes engaged in elongation, overriding the control that normally prevents interaction of the factor with ribosomes that have a peptidyl chain in the donor site.

fusidic acid interacts with ribosomes engaged either in peptide-chain elonga- tion or not, that the antibiotic forms a complex with ribosomes and GDP-EF-G and that this complex is formed by overriding the control which normally prevents EF-G interaction with ribosomes engaged on the elongation cycle.

fusidic acid interacts with the ribosome to form a fusidic acid-ribosome complex, which inhibits peptide-chain elongation and that the fusidic acid complex is formed by overriding the control mechanism that prevents EF-G interaction with ribosomes engaged on peptide-chain elongations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of fusidio acid with peptyl transfer RNA-ribosome complexes.
the mechanism by which fusidic acid inhibits peptide-chain elongation in Escherichia coli.
a new approach to the study of the mechanism of action of fusidinic acid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fusidic acid inhibits polypeptide synthesis by preventing the formation of dipeptides.

fusidic acid inhibits the EF-G-dependent GTPase activity of ribosomes, that the complex formed by this activity is involved in the inhibition of peptide-chain elongation and that, at least in the polyuridylyl-directed system, the antibiotic blocks the elongation cycle by inhibiting every step.
the antibiotic inhibits the elongation process by interfering with the EF-G-mediated translocation step.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antibiotic fusidic acid inhibits polypeptide synthesis by blocking the ribosomal accepter site, but that the block is overcome in vivo by the elongation factor.

fusidic acid inhibits the translocase function of the EF-G by forming a complex with the GDP-EF-ribosome system, and that the complex formed in the absence of aminoacyl- and peptidyltRNA is the one that inhibits polypeptide synthesis.

fusidic acid inhibits peptide-chain elongation by blocking the acceptor site of the ribosome and that the antibiotic can interact with the ribosome either directly (when the ribosome is free of aminoacyl- or peptidyll-tRNA) or indirectly (through a fusidic acid-ribosome-GDP-EF-G complex) when the donor site of the ribosomal complex is occupied by peptylidyl-tRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antibiotic inhibits the elongation process at a step subsequent to formation of the aminoacyl-t RNA ribosome complex.
fusidic acid is not an antibiotic that can be used to inhibit protein synthesis in vitro in order to study the function of elongation factors.
the fusidic acid inhibits the elongation factor G-dependent translocation step of the protein synthesis in the presence of ribosomes, peptidyl tRNA, and GTP.
